qualitative_findings.claim: bR in purple membrane transmits predominantly positively polarized electrons (spin parallel to velocity) on Au and Al, opposite in sign to dsDNA.
On Au the light helicity changes the magnitude (cw > lin > ccw) but not the sign of P.
On Al (weak SOC) no effect of light polarization; P ~15%, comparable to Au.
Full coverage gives larger P than partial coverage on Au (14% vs 5%).
Effect present for physisorbed membranes (no covalent molecule-substrate bond needed).
CV current through bR on magnetized Ni depends on magnet direction (~18%); after denaturation current drops to near zero.
Bare Ni shows reversible CV (peak separation 90 mV at 50 mV/s); bR-covered Ni is quasi-reversible with ~1 order lower current.

discrepancies.description: File '3_suppl.pdf' is the main PNAS article and '3.pdf' is the SI Appendix (names swapped).
Average stated as determined at the initial (-0.10 V) potential, but the CV initial potential is -0.05 V elsewhere (Fig. 4 caption, text).

Methods describe monolayer (15 min) and multilayer (48 h) protocols; which one each spin-polarization sample used is not stated. Fig. 2/3 samples are not linked to the SI preparation variants ('more than 10 samples').
P = 5 ± 3% (partial Au) and 15 ± 4% (Al) are given without stating the light polarization or how they were averaged; ± type undefined throughout.
S_eff given as '18%' (no sign); paper_1 used -0.229 with the same apparatus family.

extraction_meta.notes: Main = PNAS pp. 14872-14876 (uploaded as 3_suppl.pdf); SI Appendix pages 1-6 (uploaded as 3.pdf). chirality_origin omitted (not stated; enum has no 'not reported').
